name: WebUSB
plain: Lets a site talk directly to a USB device the person picks.
meaning: Reveals which USB gadgets are plugged in (vendor, product, serial number) and lets the site control them. Used for dev boards, label printers and security keys; a path to device fingerprinting.

access.prompt_ui: Browser chooser lists only devices matching filters; person selects one and clicks Connect
access.persistence: Per origin and per device until revoked; getDevices() returns previously granted devices without a prompt
access.revocation: Site settings, chooser 'forget' button, device.forget() (Chrome 101+), 'disconnect' event
access.iframe: Needs allow="usb" in cross-origin iframes; available in dedicated and service workers from Chrome 118
steps: Page does bulk, interrupt, isochronous or control transfers

data.metric: USB device descriptors plus raw data transfers
data.update: on demand; connect and disconnect events

fields.name: transfer payload
fields.range: up to 64 bytes per control transfer on low speed; bulk limited by endpoint packet size

limits.headline: Can talk to one USB device you pick from a list
limits.user_action: You tap Connect device, pick one in the chooser and click Connect.
can: Show USB devices that match what the site asks for
Connect to the one you pick
Send and get data from it, such as a flash tool or a printer
cannot: Use USB devices you did not pick
Use devices your computer already claims, like storage drives and keyboards
Work in Firefox, Safari or on iPhone
Keep access after you remove the permission or unplug it
limits.differs: Chrome and Edge, including on Android, support it. Firefox and Safari, including iPhone, do not.

story.what_it_is: A site can talk straight to a USB gadget that you pick.

marketing.name: WebUSB
marketing.pitch: Chrome's docs say WebUSB lets pages safely use USB devices, with the user in control.

story.for_you: A picker lists USB devices. You choose one and the page can set it up or talk to it, with no driver to install.
story.for_makers: Makers can ship device setup and firmware updates as a web page. It cuts support cost since there is nothing to install.

use_cases.example: A web page updates a keyboard or a microcontroller board over USB.
A web tool lets you adjust a drawing tablet's buttons.
A web based label printer app prints directly over USB.
A web page reads data from a USB glucose meter.
A web page flashes new firmware onto a game controller.
A bad site could try to talk to a USB device that holds keys or data.

technical_bounds: Cannot list devices without a user selection (filters required unless exclusionFilters/empty filters used with chooser)
Cannot claim interfaces of protected classes: HID, mass storage, audio, video, printer, smart card, wireless controller
Windows needs WinUSB driver or MS OS 2.0 descriptors; Linux needs udev rules
Not in Firefox, Safari or iOS

abuse: Fingerprinting by serial number once granted
Phishing sites mimicking a hardware setup flow

history.change: WebUSB ships (Chrome 61 stable Sep 2017, origin trial from 54)
Protected interface classes (HID, mass storage, audio, video, smart card) blocked from claim
Removed 'Serial number readable without permission' paths; granted devices persist
